headline: High prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: Devin can ingest and act on Notion content, while Notion AI can surface workspace text that Devin may treat as trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin has broad workspace and MCP access and can read files, Slack, GitHub, and browser content; Notion AI can expose workspace pages and knowledge-base text. A plausible pathway is Notion content being copied or synced into Devin’s workspace and then treated as instructions. This is not provably blocked, but it is not a direct shared channel by default.
conditions: IF Notion page content is copied into Devin’s workspace or task context without provenance labels, injection is possible.
IF Devin is instructed to follow instructions found inside workspace text, attacker-controlled Notion content can steer actions.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to imported Notion text before handing it to Devin.
Restrict Devin tasks to a fixed prompt template that ignores instructions inside retrieved content.
Use a human review step for any Notion-derived task brief.
Separate trusted task specs from untrusted workspace excerpts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch workspace content, but in different stores: Devin can access cloud workspace files and integrations, while Notion AI can access pages and databases in the user’s workspace and sends queries to vendor backends. Shared sensitive content can therefore flow through both systems, creating a realistic leakage path in default use, though not enough evidence for high or critical.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is present in both the cloud workspace and Notion workspace, both agents can process it.
IF Notion pages contain secrets or regulated data, queries may transmit that content to vendor backends.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from Notion pages and workspace files.
Use redacted copies when moving content between systems.
Limit Devin access to only the repo or folder needed for the task.
Review Notion page permissions before sharing with Devin.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write files, modify git state, and use broad cloud workspace shell access; Notion AI cannot write filesystems or modify git state and is limited to Notion-controlled actions. Overlapping write conflict is therefore limited, with the main risk being concurrent edits to shared workspace content rather than direct filesystem contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared document or task record, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF Devin mirrors Notion content into git while Notion AI edits the source page, divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each artifact.
Use branch or page locks before edits.
Have Devin pull fresh content before committing changes.
Keep Notion AI read-only for artifacts that Devin is modifying.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Devin is an autonomous planner-executor with shell and browser tools. If Devin consumes Notion AI summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or operational actions. The pathway exists in default workflows, but there is no evidence of fully automatic action chaining.
conditions: IF Devin uses Notion AI output as the sole source of truth, mistaken summaries can propagate.
IF Notion AI omits context from workspace pages, Devin may act on incomplete facts.
mitigations: Require Devin to verify Notion-derived claims against source pages.
Mark Notion AI output as draft, not authoritative.
Add a checklist item to confirm critical facts before execution.
Use citations or links back to the original Notion page.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are closed-source and vendor-hosted, but the profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch. Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens, while Notion AI processes workspace content through vendor backends; the main compliance concern is policy mismatch on sensitive workspace data, not a documented breach path.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Notion pages, it may be processed by vendor backends.
IF organizational policy forbids third-party processing of secrets, Devin’s integration tokens and Notion content handling can violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion pages used with AI.
Store secrets only in approved secret managers.
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings before use.
Restrict both agents to non-regulated workspace content.
